title: Synthetic workload generator for risk-aware batch/caching adoption
creator: Rohit Patel
description:
Goal: build a deterministic synthetic workload generator and experiment harness that produces representative traffic slices for validating batch/caching configuration changes without exposing live customers. This ticket covers generator implementation, experiment orchestration, metrics definition, dashboard panels, and automated rollback triggers.

Scope and motivation:
- Current AB experiments using split-traffic have shown economic gains but are brittle for rare tail patterns (bursts, long tokens, multimodal sequences). We need a repeatable way to simulate worst-case, typical, and edge user behavior to surface regressions early.
- This harness will let PM/Eng/Research run configurable cohorts (token-length distribution, request inter-arrival, prefix hotness) and compare cost vs SLA vs quality across candidate configs.

Deliverables:
1) Synthetic workload generator service (stateless container) with config format: workload_profile (name), qps_profile (poisson|burst|diurnal), seq_len_dist (zipf|empirical), prefix_reuse_rate, model_variant, request_size_histogram.
2) Traffic sink adapter to run in shadow mode against dedicated staging runtime and collect token-level telemetry (latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, batch occupancy, KV hit rate, kernel-fallback counts).
3) Experiment orchestration DSL (yaml) to declare candidate configs, cohort weights, duration, and guardrail thresholds.
4) Dashboards: an experiment summary board plus cohort-level detail panels for cost delta, latency risk, quality proxies (log-likelihood shift, hallucination proxy), and rollback signal charts.
5) Automated rollback playbook: hooks to routing/orchestration to revert configs if sentinel metrics cross thresholds.

Metrics (canonical list):
- cost_per_1M_tokens_delta: relative cost change vs baseline (percent)
- effective_qps: observed completed requests per second (post batching)
- batch_utilization: average occupancy / max_batch_size
- latency_p50_p95_p99_ms: percentiles at request and token granularity
- kv_cache_hit_rate: fraction of KV cache hits for prefetched prefixes
- model_quality_shift: KL divergence on token distribution + regression on eval prompts (log-likelihood change)
- rollback_rate: fraction of experiment runs that triggered automated rollback
- canary_failure_reasons: top N alerts that caused abort (latency, cost, quality)

Experiment design and analysis plan:
- Matrix: for each workload_profile × seq_len_dist × prefix_reuse_rate, run candidate config set {base, config-A (higher batching), config-B (aggressive KV-prefetch), config-C (combined)} for 4-hour windows across 3 random seeds.
- Use pairwise bootstrap to compute 95% CI on cost delta and latency p95; require non-overlap with baseline for promotion.
- Apply stratified weighting so rare but high-cost bursts (e.g., 95th token length bursts) are not drowned out by background traffic.
- Quality signals are computed against a fixed prompt corpus (200 prompts across domains). Flag if mean log-likelihood drops by >0.7 or hallucination proxy increases by >3x.

Dashboards and queries (examples):
- Experiment Summary: single-row per run (run_id, profile, config, cost_delta_pct, latency_p95_ms, quality_flag, rollback_triggered). Backend query: SELECT run_id, profile, config, AVG(cost_pct) AS cost_delta_pct, PERCENTILE(latency_ms,95) FROM experiment.telemetry WHERE run_id = $run ORDER BY run_id;
- Cohort Heatmap: x-axis seq_len_bucket, y-axis prefix_reuse_rate, cell color = avg(cost_delta_pct)
- Time-series for sentinel metrics: cost_per_1M_tokens_delta, latency_p95_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate, with horizontal thresholds set from historical baselines (+20% cost, +50ms p95).

Safety and automated rollback rules:
- Soft gate: if cost_delta_pct > +30% AND latency_p95_ms > baseline_p95 + 40ms for any 10-minute sliding window -> mark run as at-risk and notify SRE/PM via PagerDuty but do not auto-rollback.
- Hard gate (auto-rollback): if cost_delta_pct > +50% OR latency_p99_ms > baseline_p99 + 150ms OR quality_flag == true for 3 consecutive 5-minute buckets -> trigger automated rollback to previous stable config, mark run as failed, and create incident ticket template.
- Circuit breaker: only enable auto-rollback in environments with canary_cohort <= 2% traffic or in dedicated staging clusters.

Runbook for on-call when hard gate fires:
1) PagerDuty alert contains run_id, offending metric, stacktrace (if applicable), snapshot links to Grafana panels and the commit/PR that introduced the configuration.
2) On-call executes quick triage checklist (validate signal, check infra anomalies, confirm workload generator run seed).
3) If rollback occurred, verify service health and re-run minimal regression profile with reduced intensity.

Rollout plan and verification:
- Phase 1 (staging): run harness on staging dedicated fleet for 2 weeks, validate reproducibility across seeds, iterate on metric thresholds.
- Phase 2 (shadow on production): route 100% shadow traffic for chosen canary cohorts for 3 business days; compare cost/latency/quality to baseline.
- Phase 3 (small canary): 0.5%-2% live traffic with auto-rollback enabled. If stable for 7 days, increase to 5% then 20% with manual approvals.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Synthetic fidelity vs safety: higher-fidelity traces risk leaking customer data; we will use aggregated empirical distributions and synthetic sampling rather than full replay of real requests.
- Generator complexity: building a very flexible DSL increases maintenance cost; prioritize the top 6 workload shapes observed in telemetry first.
- Economic thresholds: we must balance allowed temporary cost regressions that yield long-term savings. Propose conservative default gates and enable tighter thresholds for paid-customer orgs.

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- PM: Marco Li (cost goals and biz KPIs)
- Research: Elena Martinez (eval harness and quality proxies)
- SRE: Priya Nambiar (rollback automation and runbook)
- Design: Jacob Nguyen (dashboard UX)

Acceptance criteria (must pass to mark Done):
- Generator can produce the 6 prioritized workload shapes and run controlled experiments against staging.
- Dashboards are populated automatically for every run and show the canonical metrics listed above.
- Automated hard/soft gates are implemented and tested in staging; simulated hard-gate triggers perform rollback in a dry-run mode.
- Experiment results include bootstrap CIs and a short analysis template per run (cost/latency/quality decision recommendation).

Next steps (short-term):
- [ ] Finalize workload profile list with Research (due 2026-02-27)
- [ ] Prototype generator container and runner script (due 2026-03-06)
- [ ] Create initial Grafana dashboard template and wire telemetry (due 2026-03-13)
- [ ] Add rollback automation stub to orchestration repo and open PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2741)

Long-term vision: This harness will be the canonical way we qualify any batch/caching optimization before serving it to real customers, enabling faster iteration cycles with guardrails that balance cost and reliability.
